transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Authorities in Oregon are expected to hold
a press conference next hour to provide an update
on yesterday's mass shooting at an elementary school.
A 16-year-old boy opened fire at Silver Rail Elementary,
killing three children and one teacher.
Brooke Olson is the mother of a kindergarten student there.
She tells the Associated Press
that she's in a state of disbelief.
- My thoughts are what happens now
and what can we do within our control?
Keep kids safer than ever before.
- Authorities are trying to piece together
the circumstances leading up to the attack.
Joni Auden-Land from Oregon Public Broadcasting reports.
- Soon after the shooter entered the school
by shooting off the locks on the doors,
this bystander followed them
and at some point within the next couple of minutes,
gunned them down themselves.
We still don't know who this person is
or, again, why they were at the school.
- That's Joni Auden-Land reporting.
The White House says its newest press secretary is out
and PR's Emily Fang reports that Katie Zachariah
was just days into the job.
- Asked by reporters about Zachariah,
President Trump said he gave her the option to quit.
- I said, "Katie, you know, you don't have to do this.
"You know, she said this is a lot tougher."
I said, "Welcome to the world of Trump."
- Zachariah has been careful to describe herself
as a lawyer, not an attorney,
and she ultimately admitted
that she failed the California bar exam,
meaning she is not licensed to practice law,
though Trump has referred to her as an attorney before.
Zachariah initially seemed to sidestep questions
about the bar exam, saying repeatedly
that she moved to China, where she practiced law
with, quote, "all appropriate credentials."
Zachariah later said she misheard the question.
Emily Fang and Pure News, Washington.
- New York Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez
is transferring $1 million from her campaign
to support Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed,
and PR's Elena Moore reports the Michigan Democrat
is locked in one of the most competitive matchups
of the midterms.
Ocasio-Cortez made the announcement
while campaigning alongside El-Sayed in Michigan.
- The only reason I'm doing that
is because I see the energy of each and every one of you all
stepping up to make an effort, and you all need support.
And so when you all step up, the cavalry is coming.
- The Congresswoman is a longtime ally of El-Sayed
and backed him in the Democratic primary
when many state and federal party leaders didn't.
It comes amid wide speculation
about Ocasio-Cortez's political future.
She's a prominent leader of her party's leftmost flank
and is seen as a potential 2028 presidential candidate.
Elena Moore, NPR News.
- This is NPR News in Washington.
Rights groups say that Turkey is arbitrarily arresting
and prosecuting activists at the annual UN climate summit
is about to get underway.
Turkey is hosting COP 31.
- NPR's Adil al-Shalchi reports on the arrests
at a time when activists say Turkey
has been increasing its crackdown on opposition voices.
- Human Rights Watch says Turkey's crackdown
on environmental activists is, quote,
"a salient reminder of its intolerance of dissent."
It said Turkish authorities have been forcibly dispersing
nonviolent protests using tear gas and water cannons
and finding people with random identity checks.
This comes at a time when rights groups,
including Turkey's journalists union,
say the country is stifling voices of dissent.
On Wednesday, Turkish authorities blocked a broadcaster
that is not aligned with the government.
They've also detained several journalists and academics,
particularly from LGBTQ+ groups.
This year's UN annual climate summit known as COP 31
runs for two weeks starting on November 9th.
Adil al-Shalchi, NPR News, Istanbul.
- Teenagers demanding more resources for schools in France
continue to clash with police.
Many have been arrested or injured during the protests.
Police are facing criticism over weapons described
as non-lethal that have caused serious injuries.
A police union has also filed a complaint against the state
saying officers have been put in danger.
Investigations into alleged police misconduct
are growing as President Emmanuel Macron
approaches the end of his term in May.
This is NPR News.

topics.text: Oregon elementary school shooting by a 16-year-old kills three children and a teacher; authorities await press conference
White House press secretary Katie Zachariah departs after just days on the job; she admitted failing California bar exam
Ocasio-Cortez transfers $1 million from her campaign to support Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed
Rights groups say Turkey is arbitrarily arresting and prosecuting activists ahead of UN COP 31 climate summit
Teenagers in France continue protests over school resources, clashing with police over injuries and weapons
